Wanted to add BloatNet data collection as a topic if possible.

I’d like to start conversation on the topic of passing fast confirmed block in the Engine API. Some of the questions:
* How is `safe` block used by EL clients?
* How is it used by consumers of the JSON-RPC API, e.g. exchanges, L2s etc? Whom should we reach out to get a feedback on this question?
* What do client teams prefer:
  * overload the `safe` block with the fast confirmed block (currently set to `justified`)
  * introduce a new `[fast_]confirmed` block to the Engine and JSON-RPC API
* How difficult is the latter from the engineering standpoint?

📅 ACDT Meeting 45 X/Twitter Stream: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1vOxwXMjjPmKB

📣 Promote ACDT Meeting 45 on X/Twitter: https://bit.ly/4eVLgNI

I would like to discuss the following:
1. https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/123 - To not return the full payload back to the proposer from the relay. There seems to be broad consensus  on the approach here. I want to raise it in ACDT to understand if anyone has any issues with it. 
2. https://github.com/bharath-123/builder-specs/pull/1 - We want to deprecate JSON payloads for SSZ. I want to raise it in ACDT to understand if anyone has any issues with it.

I would like to discuss why clz was bumped to 5. Analysis of other similar opcodes puts it to 3, and data is showing that it is even cheaper: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/1396813811381440512

And here is quick code in rust to compare opcodes: https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/pull/2744 it shows that clz/is_zero/mul to be similar
I would like to join the meeting to discuss the topics about ETH. How can I be part of it?
